verificationChecklist.task: Verify RDS certificate bundle with rejectUnauthorized flag
Simulate connection pool load with pgbench

riskAssessment.preventionAdvice: Do not deploy pg 8.11+ without matching AWS RDS SSL certificate bundle.

outcome.errorLogSnippet: Error: self signed certificate in certificate chain (AWS RDS Postgres:5432) at TLSSocket.onConnectSecure. Max pool size drained (25/25 clients hung).
outcome.engineerResolution: Provided AWS global-bundle.pem in ssl config and tuned pool clients to 12. Fix verified.

feedback.actualOutcomeNotes: We rushed the minor driver upgrade thinking pg 8.11 was backwards compatible. It completely broke RDS TLS handshakes.
feedback.lessonsLearned: Always verify RDS CA bundle compatibility on any pg driver change.

riskAssessment.headline: Resembles Deployment #1 pg driver RDS connection exhaustion failure
riskAssessment.summary: Deployment #27 upgrades the 'pg' driver from 8.7.3 to 8.11.3 and modifies pool configurations in checkout-api, closely mirroring Deployment #1 which caused severe 502 outages. In Deployment #1, updating pg to 8.11+ broke default TLS handshake handling against AWS RDS, causing rapid pool exhaustion under production traffic. Without explicit RDS CA bundle verification and validated keepAlive settings, this deployment risks repeating catastrophic connection drops.

historicalComparison.whatChangedThen: Upgraded 'pg' dependency from 8.7.3 to 8.11.1 in checkout-api.
historicalComparison.whatFailedThen: Strict TLS handshake failures (ECONNRESET) occurred against AWS RDS under load, exhausting the database connection pool in 4 minutes and triggering site-wide checkout 502 errors.
historicalComparison.rootCauseThen: pg v8.8+ changed default TLS rejection behaviour for self-signed or intermediate RDS certificates.
historicalComparison.resolutionThen: Configured AWS global-bundle.pem in ssl settings, set rejectUnauthorized: false with CA verification, added keepAlive: true, and reduced max pool clients to 12.
historicalComparison.outcomeThen: Database connection pool stabilized under peak traffic without ECONNRESET drops.
keyDifferences: Current target version is 8.11.3 instead of 8.11.1.
Base Docker image is being upgraded to node:20-alpine simultaneously.
PG_MAX_POOL_CLIENTS environment variable is explicitly modified in this deployment.

blastRadius.potentialImpact: Database pool starvation leading to HTTP 500/502 errors on order processing.
Halted payment capturing and retry queue accumulation.
Delayed order processing messages and downstream dispatch backlogs.
Orphaned transaction authorizations caused by dropped client connections.

verificationChecklist.task: Ensure RDS CA bundle (global-bundle.pem) is loaded in connection.ts ssl config with keepAlive enabled
Confirm PG_MAX_POOL_CLIENTS is tuned within RDS connection allocation limits (<= 12 clients per instance)
Execute synthetic connection test against RDS PostgreSQL instance matching production SSL parameters
verificationChecklist.command: node -e 'const { Pool } = require("pg"); const p = new Pool({ ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: process.env.RDS_CA_CERT } }); p.query("SELECT 1").then(() => console.log("OK")).catch(console.error).finally(() => p.end());'

riskAssessment.preventionAdvice: Halt rollout until services/checkout/src/db/connection.ts is verified against Deployment #1 fixes. Ensure the pg Pool config explicitly provides the AWS RDS global bundle CA certificate, specifies keepAlive: true, sets idleTimeoutMillis properly, and that PG_MAX_POOL_CLIENTS adheres to safe concurrency thresholds.
